source.title: Batches Stabilize the Minimum Norm Risk in High-Dimensional Overparametrized Linear Regression
source.authors: Shahar Stein Ioushua; Inbar Hasidim; Ofer Shayevitz; Meir Feder

record.file_problem: Text contains the full paper, including proofs, numerical results, discussion and references.
record.tranche_reason: The paper derives risk results for a proposed batch minimum-norm estimator in isotropic Gaussian linear regression. It discusses minibatch neural-network generalization as motivation but does not test the listed neural-network claim versions or standard gradient training on natural labels.
record.gate_note: The paper's own batch-size and risk results concern its BMN and SBMN estimators. They do not measure train-to-test error gaps, fixed-epoch minibatch training, or any other listed version. Results cited from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper studies proposed two-stage linear-regression estimators with isotropic Gaussian features. Its batch partition changes the estimator; it is explicitly different from minibatch SGD. It provides neither neural-network width experiments for V2 nor fixed-epoch image-classifier or language-model training for V5. References to these phenomena motivate the work, but its own results test none of V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate but should specify the qualification: optimized BMN has stable risk for sufficiently high SNR, whereas optimized SBMN is reported to have stable risk across SNR levels and overparametrization ratios. Batch sizes are optimized using asymptotic upper bounds. The theoretical results bound expected risk in isotropic Gaussian linear regression; simulations also show SBMN outperforming server averaging in almost all tested settings.
record.recipe_differences: Proposes a batch minimum-norm estimator and shrinkage variant for isotropic Gaussian overparametrized linear regression; not standard gradient training of neural networks. Its batches are used to build a modified regression problem, not minibatches processed under a fixed epoch budget.
record.method_sensitivity: Risk and optimal batch size vary with batch size, normalized SNR ξ, and overparametrization ratio γ. The stated BMN stability qualifications depend on SNR; SBMN removes the stated low-SNR instability.

fits_no_version.finding: BMN and SBMN have asymptotic quadratic-risk bounds depending on batch size, signal-to-noise ratio and parameter-to-sample ratio. Batch-size simulations concern BMN rather than minibatch gradient training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For isotropic Gaussian linear regression, batch minimum-norm estimation can stabilize prediction risk at sufficiently high SNR; optimized shrinkage extends the reported stability across SNR levels.

record.problems: The paper itself notes that its results are restricted to isotropic Gaussian features and expected-risk bounds; bounds can be loose, particularly near the effective interpolation point. Numerical figure values are not given in the prose.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Figure-only numeric points were not extracted; qualitative trends stated in the text are recorded in R4.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out accuracy in the same neural-network training recipes.
Held-out error as neural-network width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects in image classifiers or language models under fixed epoch budgets, including recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on classifier held-out error, including interactions with training-set size and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps among convolutional networks.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized versus randomly selected training examples.

record.verdict_notes: All four rows remain outside the listed versions. Increasing parameter-to-sample ratio in this linear estimator is not a test of V2's neural-network width claim. Batch partitioning here is not V5's minibatch training intervention. No version-specific verdicts or missing results are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels alongside generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers and their held-out performance.
Large-batch training under fixed epoch budgets in image classifiers and language models.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: BMN estimator
rows.size_stated: n samples and p parameters; limit n,p → ∞ with γ = p/n fixed
rows.operation_detail: Derived asymptotic quadratic-risk bounds for the batch minimum-norm estimator as a function of batch size, normalized SNR and overparametrization ratio.
rows.measure: Asymptotic normalized quadratic risk R(β̂ BMN)
rows.note: The result is a bound on parameter/prediction quadratic risk in a theoretical linear-regression model, not a measured train-test gap.
rows.check: The excess-noise term is mistranscribed. The upper bound is (γb−1)/(γb+(b−1)ξ) + ((1−ξ)/ξ)·(b−(b−1)ξ)/(γb−1). The lower bound replaces the first term with (1−1/(γb))^(1+(b−1)ξ) and multiplies the noise term by Cγ,ξ,b. These estimator-risk bounds measure no listed version.

rows.subject: BMN estimator with optimized batch size
rows.size_stated: n samples and p parameters; limit n,p → ∞ with γ = p/n fixed
rows.operation_detail: Optimized batch size by minimizing the upper bound on asymptotic risk.
rows.measure: Optimal batch size from upper-bound minimization; asymptotic risk behavior
rows.baseline: b = 1 / standard min-norm comparison discussed in paper
rows.value: The optimal batch size b → ∞; in this region BMN behaves similarly to min-norm, producing phenomena such as double-descent and local risk minima. When SNR < 1, BMN can have normalized risk ≥ 1.
rows.note: The batch-size optimization is theoretical and concerns the proposed estimator, not a fixed-epoch minibatch-training comparison.
rows.check: The selected batch size minimizes an asymptotic upper bound, rather than proven exact risk; this selection value should not itself be a result row. Separate it from the risk discussion. The text includes ξ≤0.6478, and its double-descent discussion concerns the optimized upper bound. Finite-sample optimal batch sizes remain finite.

rows.subject: SBMN estimator with optimized batch size
rows.size_stated: n samples and p parameters; limit n,p → ∞ with γ = p/n fixed
rows.operation_detail: Derived asymptotic risk bounds for the shrinkage batch minimum-norm estimator.
rows.measure: Asymptotic normalized quadratic risk R(β̂ SBMN)
rows.baseline: Null risk and min-norm are comparison estimators discussed in the paper
rows.note: The paper states that optimized SBMN risk is monotonically increasing in γ and at least as good as null risk for all SNR levels; it does not measure a train-test gap.
rows.check: The recorded formula incorrectly combines the lower-bound bias with the upper-bound variance. Theorem 4 gives upper bound (γb−1)/(γb+(b−1)ξ) + (1−ξ)/(γb−1); its lower bound is (1−1/(γb))^(1+(b−1)ξ) + ((1−ξ)/(γb−1))·Cγ,ξ,b. This theorem concerns arbitrary admissible b, not specifically an optimized estimator.

rows.subject: BMN and SBMN estimators
rows.size_stated: Numerical experiment with n = 1000 for Figure 8; other experiment sizes not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared estimator risk across batch sizes in numerical experiments.
rows.baseline: Other tested batch sizes; exact numeric baselines not stated
rows.value: For ξ = 0.5 and 0.6, risk monotonically decreases with b; for ξ = 0.7 and 0.8 the optimal batch size is b > 1; for ξ = 0.9 the minimal risk is obtained at b = 1.
rows.note: The text states the qualitative trends; plotted values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Figure 8 tests BMN only, not SBMN. Its caption indicates varying signal energy r² and different null risks across scenarios, so these plotted risks should not be described as normalized risk without qualification. The stated within-scenario batch-size trends are correctly extracted. This is performance evaluation of the proposed estimator, not evidence for V5.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
